newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Reinsurance chief warns on future industry change.
newsitem.headline: Reinsurance chief warns on future industry change.

text.p: There will be more consolidation in the international reinsurance industry, but it will not necessarily happen for the right reasons, Employers Re chief executive Kaj Ahlmann told a conference on Tuesday.

"All the major players have sufficient global presence to service their customers, so it does not make strategic sense to acquire more companies at a high premium unless you know what you want to achieve," Ahlmann told a London International Insurance and Reinsurance Market Association (LIRMA) conference.
"Insurance acquisitions should not be driven by investment bankers," he said.
Ahlmann predicted that between 45 and 50 percent of the world's reinsurance market would be in the hands of the top four players following more than $26 billion worth of acquisitions in 1996.
The leading companies include Munich Re, Swiss Re and U.S.-based Employers Re.
However, Ahlmann said the strategic reasons for acquisition were running out.
"There are no direct reinsurance writers left, and broker-based reinsurers add little value to direct reinsurers. In addition there are few franchises to be had," he told the conference.
Ahlmann said that future trends included growth of alternative risk transfer, the increasing importance of technology and expansion in the life and health insurance markets.
"The name of the game has changed and will continue to change. Only those who understand this will stay on top," he said.
